headline: Does bone age tell you
subhead: HOW MUCH GROWTH YOU HAVE LEFT?

headline: So first
subhead: WHERE DOES THE NUMBER EVEN COME FROM?
body: Bone age is read from a hand and wrist X-ray. Then that one number gets applied to your whole skeleton to predict remaining growth. | The idea only works if the hand is on the same schedule as the legs, and as we will see it is not even close.
punch: The hand is not the legs.

headline: First study
body: The study looked at when different bones in the same animal fuse. In mice, *epiphyseal fusion* happened at about **3 weeks** in the phalanges and **4 weeks** in the metacarpals but had not yet occurred at **12 weeks** in tibias or femurs. | Many of you will think this is a mouse thing, which is wrong because they repeated it in rats: **12 weeks** phalanges, **16 weeks** metacarpals, tibia and femur still open.

headline: And now
body: The same study showed that the hand bones do not just fuse earlier, they grow slower the entire time. At one week, metacarpal growth rate was **49%** of the tibial rate and *proliferation per column* was **46%**. | Every marker of *growth plate senescence*, which is the plate running out of divisions, was more advanced in the metacarpals and phalanges than in the femur and tibia.
punch: ==Your hand is further through the process than your legs. Always.==

headline: Breakthrough insight
subhead: IT IS THE SIGNAL, NOT THE BONE
body: This is the part i found genuinely interesting. They isolated *chondrocytes* from finger bones and leg bones. Finger cells proliferated slower. Then they added IGF-1 to the finger cells and proliferation rose **to match untreated leg cells**. | So the small bones are not built differently. They receive less growth signal, and when you give it back the difference disappears.
punch: The difference is IGF signalling reaching the plate.

headline: Second study
body: Now with the second study we move to humans. MRI of the wrist, knee and ankle in **958 people** aged 14 to 21. Fusion timing varied by site inside the same person and complete fusion happened about **2 years earlier** in girls than boys. | *Pubertal stage* correlated with fusion at every site, **0.514 to 0.598** in males.
punch: _One body, several closure dates, and puberty stage tracks all of them._

headline: And this is why
body: The same study tested physical activity directly. No significant correlation in males at any site. In females one very low correlation at the wrist, **0.095**, and nothing else. | **BMI** on the other hand did correlate, 0.186 to 0.384. So the thing everyone tells you to do for your plates did not move them, and body composition did.

headline: So
subhead: WHAT DO YOU ACTUALLY DO WITH THIS
body: Read bone age as an estimate from your fastest ageing bones, not your legs. Track pubertal stage, which is what actually correlated. And stop treating training as the thing that closes your plates, because in 958 people it was not.
punch: The hand finishes first. Every time.
